neighbours.label: A preposition marking where something is found or done in a local crime or incident report (the butt of a pistol, found under a porch, rummaged through the jeep); calm scenes read lower
fire: The clerk was hit in the face with the butt of a rifle.
Deputies went to a farm to check a dead horse found under a bridge.
A stranger rummaged through the trunk of the patrol car.
The thief was struck on the arm with the handle of a shovel.
Officers found a stolen wallet under a parked truck.
A masked man searched through the drawers of the office.
Police recovered the gun from under a porch on Oak Street.
The victim was beaten with the end of a pool cue.
quiet: The clerk was given a card with the name of a shop.
Children went to a farm to see a new horse in a field.
A stranger smiled at the driver of the bus.
The girl read a book under a tree by the lake.
Friends found a nice cafe near a quiet park.
A tired man sat at the desk of the office.
Neighbours held a party on a porch on Oak Street.
The winner was given a trophy at the end of the game.

notes: 'read a book under a tree' read 0.31, so one calm 'under' is kept as a near miss.
